//: Runtime knobs that have no MSBuild property. These are merged into
CounterStrikeSharp.API.runtimeconfig.json at build/publish time, which is the
config the native host hands to hostfxr (src/scripting/dotnet_host.cpp).
Everything here is overridable at launch with a DOTNET_* env var, so an operator
can A/B a value on a live server without rebuilding CSSharp.
GC mode itself (Workstation vs Server) is set from the csproj -- see the long
comment there for why this fork runs Workstation + background GC.

//System.GC.RetainVM: Keep freed GC segments mapped instead of releasing them back to the OS.
A CS2 server allocates in waves (round start, map load) and would otherwise
munmap/mmap the same memory every cycle, paying page faults and kernel time on
the game thread to re-fault it in. Costs a little RSS, removes that churn.
//System.GC.DynamicAdaptationMode: DATAS. Only meaningful under Server GC (it tunes heap count at runtime); it is
explicitly off so that a DOTNET_gcServer=1 experiment gets a fixed, predictable
heap count rather than a heap count that drifts under load. If you do switch to
Server GC, also pin System.GC.HeapCount (e.g. 2-4) and set System.GC.NoAffinitize
to true so GC threads are not hard-bound to cores the engine's own threads need.
//System.Runtime.TieredCompilation.Quick: Tier-0 compile methods containing loops too, instead of going straight to the
optimising JIT. Startup and first-hit paths (map change, first round, a plugin's
first command) stop stalling the game thread on full JIT; TieredPGO still
re-compiles anything hot to fully optimised code afterwards.
